quirks.summary: Under load the portal returns a 'Too Many Requests' page as a VALID PDF (1,164 bytes), so magic-byte verification passes on files that contain no document.
quirks.detail: Observed 2026-09-20 during a document pull on a major application. Twenty-one consecutive file GETs returned an identical 1,164-byte %PDF- file whose text is the rate-limit notice. HTTP status, content type and magic bytes are all indistinguishable from a real download; the identical file size was the only signal. After a 90-second backoff and a correctly re-established session chain, the documents tab itself returned the same stub. Separately, a file GET made without the documents tab having been loaded in that session returns HTTP 404 'Document Unavailable' — ordinary Idox session gating, but it presents as a portal fault.
quirks.workaround: Pace at 5s+ on this install and never run a download batch concurrently with other requests to the same host. Verify by size and extracted text, not magic bytes alone. On a second rate-limit, stop and hand over browser links.

quirks.summary: WAF signals present (cloudflare) but the landing page served normally.
quirks.detail: Passive at survey time. Not a reason to avoid the automated route; it is a reason to pace properly and to expect a challenge if you do not.

quirks.summary: The advanced search offers no 'application received' date filter; use date(applicationValidatedStart/End) instead.
quirks.detail: Posting date(applicationReceivedStart) to an install that does not offer it returns HTTP 500, which reads as a portal fault rather than a bad parameter. Fields present: appealDecision, applicationCommittee, applicationDecision, applicationValidated.
quirks.workaround: Read the date field names off the advanced search form before posting.

verification.note: Landing-page survey 2026-09-16: HTTP 200; vendor confirmed by fingerprint (idox-public-access); WAF signals: cloudflare
End-to-end: advanced search over 1-31 July 2026 -> first result -> documents tab (15 file links) -> downloaded one file, 64520 bytes, magic bytes 255044462d312e35 = pdf.

Recipe C fast path worked first time on a 1,743-row major application: search -> keyVal -> documents tab -> download with Referer, 13 substantial documents retrieved (largest 10.7MB). A later batch hit the rate limit and returned the 1,164-byte 'Too Many Requests' PDF on 21 consecutive GETs; handed over browser links per the stop rule. Difficulty raised routine -> fragile on that basis.
